user_saw: While following logs, users could miss newly appended records if the log file was truncated during a read and regrew before the next poll.
summary: The log-tail reader now advances its cursor to the byte after the last newline it actually read.
reasoning: I checked the reader before July’s short-read fix and found that it already sampled file size before opening the file and assigned `cursor = size` even when the read returned fewer bytes. The August blame candidate preserved that behavior for newline-terminated reads. The available path history stops at the July 1 shallow boundary because an older object is missing, so I could not verify when the defect was introduced.
